features.description: In tools/nightly_classify.py, split the one overloaded set into two. Keep INFRA_CATEGORIES = {api_error, timeout, executor_error} EXACTLY as-is (it drives infra_tainted() -> persistent_failures(), i.e. per-BENCH filing suppression). Add RUN_UNMEASURED_CATEGORIES = INFRA_CATEGORIES | {non_agentic, quota_exhausted, rate_limit, cost_killed}, used ONLY by run_validity(). Discriminator, taken from the taxonomy's own comments: a category belongs in the run-level set iff it means 'the harness did not obtain a measurement of the subject' (metrics.go:180 quota_exhausted 'says nothing about the model's capability'; :181 rate_limit transient 429; :182 cost_killed eval-side budget; error_categorizer.go:5-9 non_agentic 'or a tool-delivery problem'). Categories that ARE measurements of the subject stay out and must remain gateable-through: compile_error, runtime_error, logic_error, verify_error, constraint_violation, refused, step_exhausted, thrash_aborted, resource_limit (metrics.go:186 'A model failure (unbounded allocation)'). No signature change, no history dependency, no new flag. Add tests in a new RunGateTests class.

features.description: This is the SECOND filing of the same class of gap (#524 -> #551): the Go producer's error-category taxonomy and the Python consumer's classification sets drift silently, and nothing notices. Per CLAUDE.md section 3 (SYSTEMIC FIXES — AUDIT BEFORE PATCHING), fix the pattern rather than the single case. Precedent exists in-file: test_Vocabulary_every_python_reason_exists_in_validity_go already reads validity.go from Python. Harvest 'ErrorCategory[A-Za-z0-9_]* = "..."' from internal/eval_harness/metrics.go and internal/eval_harness/error_categorizer.go and assert every harvested value is classified in EXACTLY ONE of RUN_UNMEASURED_CATEGORIES, a new explicit MODEL_OUTCOME_CATEGORIES, or {'none'}. Verified runnable at plan time: 16 Go categories harvested, all 16 classify, 0 overlap, exactly 1 Python-only extra. That extra, 'executor_error', is a PHANTOM — no Go code anywhere in the repo emits it; it lives only in Python and design docs. Pin it in an explicit KNOWN_PYTHON_ONLY = {'executor_error'} allowlist with that comment and DO NOT remove it (behaviour change with no evidence). Finally raise the CI anti-vacuity floor.
